findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? instead of unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric field value
findings.failure_mode: corrupt or malformed audit data causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use ? on parse with map_err to convert to a domain error type

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast on parse::<u32>() result silently truncates values outside u16 range (0-65535)
findings.failure_mode: values 65536-4294967295 silently wrap to 0-65535, producing incorrect records with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>()?) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing into a Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g. empty line, trailing newline) causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) returning Option, or match on parts with a length guard, and return typed errors for missing fields

findings.problem: println! side effect embedded in the data-processing pipeline (inside the map closure)
findings.failure_mode: side effects make the function impure, break determinism, prevent unit testing, and cause duplicate log output if the function is called in loops or retries
findings.fix: move I/O/printing to a shell layer; the core parsing function should return data only with no stdout side effects

findings.problem: load_audits performs I/O (fs::read_to_string) and returns Vec<Record> instead of Result, hiding all fallible operations
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish success from I/O failure, parse failure, or malformed data — all are silently panics
findings.fix: declare fn load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError> where AuditError is an enum covering Io and Parse variants

findings.problem: name: String is a raw primitive type with no domain constraints
findings.failure_mode: any arbitrary string including empty, whitespace-only, or invalid characters is accepted without domain-level validation
findings.fix: introduce a newtype AuditName(String) with a fallible constructor that validates non-empty and valid characters

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or latency
no profiler data for allocation profile of the CSV parsing path
no allocation audit (try_reserve not used; intermediate Vec<String> collected per line)
no second-ring validation strategy for audit file format
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. All four unwrap() sites are panic vectors on untrusted input. The lossy as cast silently corrupts data. Unchecked indexing panics on malformed lines. The function mixes I/O, logging, and parsing with no error propagation — a single corrupt line crashes the entire load.
